chapters.summary: Chair Pierina Ana Sanchez calls the meeting to order, introduces herself as Chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings, and announces the committee will vote on Intro 839A, which makes the Certification of No Harassment Program permanent and adds criteria for building inclusion.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez opens hearing and introduces Intro 839A

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Sergeant, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I am Councilmember, still morning.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Pierina-Ana-Sanchez, Chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, the committee will be voting on Intro No.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: 839A, which would make the Certification of No Harassment Program permanent and add criteria for inclusion of certain buildings in that program.

chapters.summary: Sanchez explains that every tenant deserves to live free from harassment regardless of citizenship status, and that it is unlawful for landlords to retaliate against tenants for exercising their rights, such as calling 311 about a rat infestation.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez on tenant harassment and landlord retaliation

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Every tenant deserves to live free from harassment, regardless of their citizenship status.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: In New York City, it is unlawful for landlords to retaliate against tenants for exercising their rights as tenants.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When a tenant is suffering from a rat infestation in their apartment, for example, it is unlawful for the tenant harassment, for the landlord, excuse me, to punish them for calling 311.

chapters.summary: Sanchez highlights how federal mass deportation policies make immigrant New Yorkers particularly vulnerable to retaliation, noting dangerous and unique forms of harassment targeting immigrant communities.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez on immigrant tenants facing deportation threats

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, as the federal government carries out a program of mass deportation and intimidation, immigrant New Yorkers are particularly vulnerable to threats of retaliation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: They face dangerous and unique forms of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And here in our city, we have unfortunately seen a pattern of mistreatment.

chapters.summary: Sanchez details three cases: a landlord fined $17,000 for threatening to call ICE, a Queens/Long Island management company paying $55,000 for posting signs encouraging tenants to report immigrants, and Sunnyside tenants threatened with deportation for requesting basic repairs.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez cites specific harassment cases involving ICE threats

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For example, a landlord who threatened to call ICE on an undocumented tenant was fined $17,000 after a CCHR complaint.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: A Queens and Long Island-based management company agreed to pay $55,000.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: After state officials found that the company posted a sign in its lobby encouraging tenants to report immigrants to federal authorities.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And in Sunnyside, Queens, there were reports of being harassed, intimidated, and even threatened with deportation simply for requesting basic repairs.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: At a time when the federal government is targeting immigrant communities, we must ensure that all of our neighbors receive the strongest possible protections.

chapters.summary: Sanchez states the council will vote on 839A to make the CONH program permanent and stronger, responding to rising reports of landlords threatening to call ICE on tenants by expanding the definition of harassment.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez outlines 839A: making CONH permanent and stronger

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The council will vote on 839A, which will make the certification of no harassment program permanent and stronger.

chapters.summary: Sanchez explains the CONH program was created in 2018 to deter owners from using construction to harass and displace tenants, and that after two successful pilots it has proven effective at identifying high-risk buildings and deterring bad actors.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez on CONH program history and pilot success

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The CONH program was first created in 2018 to deter owners from using construction to harass and displace tenants from their homes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And after two successful pilots, CONH has proven itself to be useful for identifying high-risk buildings and deterring bad actors.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, we build on that success by codifying CONH as a permanent tool in the city's enforcement toolkit.

chapters.summary: Sanchez describes specific bill provisions: expanding the harassment definition to include ICE threats, monitoring problematic portfolios by reviewing buildings with the same owners as those with harassment findings, and creating stronger incentives to clear violations by requiring significant improvements before exiting the program.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez details bill provisions: harassment definition, portfolio monitoring, exit incentives

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Specifically, the bill will respond to rising reports of landlords threatening to call ICE on their tenants by expanding the definition of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The bill will monitor problematic portfolios by reviewing all buildings that have the same owner as those with findings of harassment.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And the bill will create stronger incentives to clear violations by allowing buildings to exit the program, only if those owners are significantly improving living conditions for their tenants.

chapters.summary: Sanchez clarifies that the bill explicitly allows basic maintenance to continue without delay for any building in the program, preempting criticism that CONH prevents basic repairs. She emphasizes that only building changes historically used to harass tenants are restricted.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez clarifies basic maintenance still allowed under CONH

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill will clarify that basic maintenance continues to be allowed without delay for any building in the program.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And colleagues, this is the thing that will be lodged at you about the

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Oh, now we can't do basic repairs because of the CONH program.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That is false.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Basic repairs are still allowed.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We're talking about changes to a building, to a residence that have been used in the past to harass tenants.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks the coalition of advocates including ANHD whose testimony made the legislation possible, the HPD team that stewarded the program through pilot phases, and former Council Member Brad Lander who led passage of the original CONH pilot in 2018.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez acknowledges advocates, HPD, and Brad Lander

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Before we vote, I just want to take a moment to acknowledge first the coalition of advocates whose testimony and partnership made this legislation possible 10 years ago and also today,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: especially in ANHD, the HPD team who have stewarded this program through its pilot phases and negotiated this legislation in good faith, and former council member,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: then controller, and future congressman, Brad Lander, who led the passage of the original CONH pilot back in 2018.

chapters.summary: Sanchez recognizes committee staff members by name including Austin Malone, Billy Eck, Mark Chen, Jose Conde, Dirk Spencer, Carla Naranjo, Reese Hirota, Noah Slosberg, and Mohamed Shadid for their work on the legislation.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez thanks Housing and Buildings Committee staff

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'd also like to thank the Housing and Buildings Committee staff, Austin Malone, Billy Eck, Mark Chen, Jose Conde, Dirk Spencer, Carla Naranjo, Reese Hirota, Noah Slosberg, and Mohamed Shadid.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks her personal staff including Deputy Chief of Staff Ben Ratner who she credits as holding the legislation as his 'legislative baby,' Deputy Chief Kim Castellano, District Director Maria Jose Mares, Gerard Fernandez, scheduler Dylan Campos, fellow, district team members Soraya Bonilla and Oriana Roa Acevedo, and intern Jacob Hayward.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez thanks her personal office team

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And finally, I'd like to take this opportunity to thank my team, especially Deputy Chief of Staff Ben Ratner, who held this piece of legislation as your legislative baby.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Congratulations.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Our Deputy Chief Kim Castellano, District Director Maria Jose Mares, Gerard Fernandez, our scheduler Dylan Campos, our fellow, our district team Soraya Bonilla and Oriana Roa Acevedo, and our intern who is here today, Jacob Hayward.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You are all here today.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm so excited to have you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You saw what it took to get here.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you for your role in this.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And with that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Unless colleagues have any comments, I'd like to ask the clerk to...

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Call the roll.

chapters.summary: Committee Clerk William Martin conducts the roll call. Chair Sanchez votes aye, followed by Council Members Riley, Feliz, Abreu, Hudson, Williams, Salaam, and Wilson all voting aye. Council Member Zhuang abstains and Council Member Maloney votes aye.

chapters.summary: The clerk announces the bill passes with 9 in the affirmative, 0 in the negative, and 1 abstention. Chair Sanchez thanks colleagues for their support and closes the committee meeting.
chapters.title: Vote result: 9-0-1, Intro 839A approved by committee

utterances.speaker: William Martin

summary: The Committee on Housing and Buildings voted on Intro 839A, making the Certification of No Harassment (CONH) pilot program permanent and expanding harassment definitions to include ICE-related threats against immigrant tenants.

Chair Pierina Ana Sanchez detailed the bill's provisions: expanding the definition of harassment, monitoring problematic owner portfolios, strengthening exit incentives, and clarifying that basic maintenance remains allowed.
The bill passed 9-0 with one abstention (Council Member Zhuang), codifying CONH as a permanent enforcement tool first piloted in 2018.
title: Committee on Housing and Buildings
topic: Making the certification of no harassment pilot program permanent and adding criteria for inclusion of certain buildings in the program
